topic: Revision of orders prejudicial to the revenue
question: Explain the power of the Principal Commissioner or Commissioner of Income-tax under section 263 to revise an order that is erroneous and prejudicial to the interests of the revenue.
keywords: prejudicial to the interests of the revenue
sources: Malabar Industrial Co. Ltd. v. CIT (Supreme Court)

points.label: Twin conditions
points.description: The order must be both erroneous and prejudicial to the interests of the revenue; if only one condition is met, it cannot be revised. Where the Assessing Officer has taken one of two possible views, the order is not erroneous merely because the Commissioner prefers the other view.
points.basis: Income-tax Act, 1961, section 263(1), as explained by the Supreme Court in Malabar Industrial Co. Ltd. v. CIT

points.label: Procedure and powers
points.description: The Commissioner may call for and examine the records of any proceeding and, after giving the assessee an opportunity of being heard and making any inquiry needed, may enhance or modify the assessment, cancel it, or direct a fresh assessment.

points.label: Orders deemed erroneous
points.description: An order is deemed erroneous and prejudicial if it was passed without the inquiries or verification that should have been made, allows relief without inquiring into the claim, is not in line with a Board order or instruction under section 119, or is not in line with a binding decision of the jurisdictional High Court or the Supreme Court.

points.label: Matters decided in appeal
points.description: Where the order has been the subject of an appeal, the revision power extends only to matters that were not considered and decided in that appeal.
keywords: not considered and decided in appeal

points.label: Time limit and appeal
points.description: No revision order can be passed after two years from the end of the financial year in which the order sought to be revised was passed; the assessee can appeal against the revision order to the Income-tax Appellate Tribunal.
